requirements.text: my colleague Joseph Johnson is unable to access the portal to view our assets ... ensure he is associated with this new ticket so he receives all updates
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact WHERE contact_id = 125 AND account_id = 9 AND portal_user_id = 610 AND active = 1 AND is_primary = 0
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; the task creates one contact
creating the contact is implied by the request, not stated: Joseph Johnson has no contact record, and one linked to Wonka Industries is what lets him see the account's assets and be named on the case
Joseph Johnson is user_id 610 (joseph.johnson@wonkaindustries.com, the only Joseph Johnson; active, role customer), so his profile needs no change
account_id 9 is Wonka Industries, the account of the requester Allen Martin (contact 12)
active 1: he is to use the portal and receive updates; kept from the benchmark check
is_primary 0: kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy; Allen Martin's contact 12 is already the account's primary contact

requirements.text: Please create a priority case through the website for this piece of hardware immediately
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 9 AND contact_id = 125 AND installed_product_id = 48 AND channel = 'web' AND priority = 'critical' AND state = 'new'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; the task creates one case
installed_product_id 48 is account 9's only flash storage array (Pure Storage FlashArray//X Variant 23, in_use) at the Sydney site
priority critical from 'critical outage' and 'priority case'
state new: the policy's default state for a new case
contact_id 125: a case holds one contact, and associating Joseph Johnson so he receives updates means his new contact is the case's contact

notes:
The two independent passes agree on every requirement, value and disposition; no disagreement to resolve.
Both benchmark checks return a column value compared with an id; the requirements test the same predicates as counts.
'Check if his user profile is active' is a read: user 610 is already active, so nothing is written to the user table. The requester's email is for clarifications only and writes nothing.
The case's product_id is not tested: the policy asks for a product or an installed product, and if a product is set it must be 155, the installed product's product. The short description is left out: only the policy's template fixes it, and the benchmark does not test it.
The account has an active account-wide entitlement (79, unlimited) and an active entitlement for product 155 (82, ten cases a month), both under active contract 24, so nothing blocks the case.
